archetype.name: Bubble Team (goalie-carried)
archetype.definition: A team whose winning start rests on one goalie stopping almost everything, while its 5-on-5 play and power play look like a club fighting for a wild-card spot rather than a division title.

report.headline: Ullmark is holding up a 6-3 start the underlying play hasn't earned
report.take:
Ottawa's 6-3-0 looks like a team that has figured things out. The goal line says otherwise: 24 scored and 23 allowed, a +1 differential that ranks 15th per game, and a site rank of 16th of 32. The Senators sit third in the Atlantic on record, but their Pts vs Goal Diff of 1.6 is fourth-highest in the league. Several of the wins have been one-goal games, and both overtime games went their way. That is a record running ahead of the margin.

The driver is Linus Ullmark. His .945 save % and 7.8 GSAx in seven starts make him fourth on the goalie tab, and they explain how a team allowing a league-average 26 shots a game ranks eighth in goals against. Everything around him is soft. Ottawa takes 44% of 5-on-5 shot attempts (27th), gets 48.8% of the expected goals, and puts only 23.1 shots a game on net (29th), more than four below the league. The power play converts at 12.8%, 27th, against a league average around 20%. Tim Stützle has 12 points and has carried the scoring almost alone. Dylan Cozens has 18 shots and no goals, and the forward group grades a C.

History gives the story a twist. Last season Ottawa drove play: 55.6% xGF, 53% CF and an eighth-ranked offense. It was sunk by goaltending worth -24 GSAx. This year the two have traded places. The goaltending fix is real while Ullmark is in net, but the territorial game has fallen off sharply. Samuel Ersson's two starts (.829, -4.2 GSAx) show how thin the margin is when Ullmark sits.

The recent stretch is already leaking. Over the last five games Ottawa went 3-2-0 and was outscored 14-12, allowing more per game than its season rate. The 109-point pace will not hold. If Ullmark stays elite and the power play recovers toward last year's 24%, this is a playoff team. If either slips, it is a bubble team that has banked a cushion early.

strengths.title: Ullmark is stealing games
strengths.body: Ullmark's .945 save % and 7.8 GSAx are the whole defensive story. They turn average shot volume against into the league's eighth-best goals-against rate. No goalie keeps a .945 over a season, so expect regression, but even a strong-not-spectacular Ullmark is a real upgrade on last season's -24 team GSAx.

strengths.title: Stützle driving the top line
strengths.body: Stützle has 12 points and a team-best 9.5 Game Score while playing over 22 minutes a night. His 52.7% xGF suggests he is winning his minutes, not just finishing. That production is the most sustainable thing in the attack.

strengths.title: Defense limits centers and defensemen
strengths.body: Opposing centers and defensemen have been held under their expected output: rank 6 against centers, rank 3 against defensemen. Thomas Chabot's 25-plus minutes at a 52.6% xGF anchor a blueline graded B-.

concerns.title: Losing the puck at 5-on-5
concerns.body: A 44% CF and 23.1 shots a game put Ottawa near the bottom of the league in possession and volume. That is a steep fall from last season's 53% CF and 55.6% xGF. Unless the team recovers its old shape, it is relying on goaltending to cover a structural shortfall.

concerns.title: Power play has gone cold
concerns.body: At 12.8%, the power play sits 27th, a long way from the 24% it ran last season. With 5-on-5 offense this thin, the man advantage was supposed to be where goals came from. Some bounce-back is likely given the track record.

concerns.title: Record ahead of the margin
concerns.body: Ottawa has a +1 goal differential and a Pts vs Goal Diff of 1.6, fourth in the league, built on close wins. The defense has also leaked to wingers (rank 27), with wingers taking far more than the league share of points against. The last five games already show the results slipping toward the underlying numbers.

trend.note: A 3-0 opening run gave way to a 3-2-0 last five in which Ottawa was outscored. Lopsided losses to Detroit and St. Louis showed how quickly things turn when the saves dry up.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, then Vegas: a stern test of the start
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Florida, a sixth-ranked team that controls 58% of 5-on-5 shot attempts. That is exactly the kind of opponent that exposes Ottawa's possession problem. San Jose the next night is the soft spot: 24th on the site, a 40.8% xGF and a 94.5 PDO. Its 4-3-1 record leans on a league-leading Pts vs Goal Diff of 2.2. With a back-to-back, though, one of these games may go to Ersson.

The Rangers arrive with an A+ goaltending grade, a 93.5% penalty kill and a defense that has held forwards furthest under expectation outside one team. Goals will be scarce for a power play running at 12.8%. The trip to Vegas closes the week against the league's best goal differential and an A+ forward group. Two of four points from the first three games would be acceptable; anything from Vegas is a bonus.

keyMatchups.title: Florida's puck control vs Ottawa
keyMatchups.body: Florida's 58% CF and 29.2 shots a game meet an Ottawa team taking 44% of attempts. Expect Ullmark to face heavy volume. Whether he can keep stealing those games is the week's central question.

keyMatchups.title: Struggling power play vs Rangers' kill
keyMatchups.body: New York kills 93.5% of penalties, second in the league, and its goaltending grades A+. Ottawa's 27th-ranked power play is unlikely to break through. A low-event, coin-flip game is the realistic hope.

keyMatchups.title: Vegas forwards vs a winger leak
keyMatchups.body: Ottawa has been worst at containing wingers (rank 27 against them). Vegas brings an A+ forward group, a third-ranked offense and a 13.8% shooting rate. That is the matchup most likely to blow up the goals-against line.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts the San Jose back-to-back. Ersson's .829 makes even the week's easiest game a risk.

restOfSeason.body:
The 109-point pace is a product of Ullmark's start and close-game luck, and both will cool. The Senators' underlying numbers from last season were strong. If their 5-on-5 play recovers toward that level while Ullmark stays above average, they are a legitimate playoff team. If this year's possession numbers are real and Ullmark drifts toward normal, they settle near the middle of the pack.

The power play should improve from 12.8%, since this core ran near 24% last year. Shooting at 10.6% is already below the league, so finishing is not inflating anything. The save percentage is the number that has to come down. I project somewhere around 90-100 points: in the wild-card race, not the division race.

confidence.note: Nine games; the goaltending and close-game results are especially noisy at this sample.
